learningObjectiveItems.title: Learning Objectives
learningObjectiveItems.learningObjective: This learning lab will enable you to explore specific aspects of the following chapter objectives within the context of a typical healthcare scenario:
learningObjectivesList: Explain how ethics differ from laws and how ethics are an important consideration in providing quality patient care.
Describe the concepts of patient rights and privileged communications and the legislation and procedures that are put into practice to ensure confidentiality of healthcare information.

introductionList: You are a student athletic trainer who is completing an internship with the Mustangs, a local professional baseball team. In this activity, you will face several scenarios that test your ability to make legal and ethical decisions. Your task is to choose the most appropriate course of action in each scenario.
introduction.mode: Learning Mode: This is a practice activity with hints available at each step.

STEP_1.instructions: You just finished a stretching and ice bath treatment on Manny Garcia, one of the team players. As you are writing up the documentation of his treatment, you overhear Manny talking to one of the team's coaches.
instructionsList: Review the conversation between Manny and the team coach.
To listen to the conversation, select the audio button beneath the chat bubbles.
Choose your next course of action from the three options provided at the bottom of the screen.
To get tips on how to proceed, select the hint option in the responses panel.

conversation.title: Team Coach
conversation.text: Manny, it might be time to consider retiring. You've been playing for over 15 years, and your stamina just isn't the same. Recovery from your shoulder surgery has been tough. The owner's already talking with the manager about letting you go.

conversation.title: Manny Garcia
conversation.text: I just don't think that I am ready to give all of this up. The doctor has advised that I stop playing but it has been my life for so long. What else can I do?

STEP_1.question: What should you do with the information you just overheard?
STEP_1.INCORRECT_1: You take out your phone and send a text to your best friend that you just heard that Garcia is about to be cut or retire from the team. You feel safe doing so since you are not posting the information to a public site.
STEP_1.CORRECT: You decide, in the moment, to not share the information you have heard. Relevant information will be shared by officials when the time is right.
STEP_1.INCORRECT_2: You make a mental note to share this information with your best friend later in private. You are confident that you and your best friend can keep this information safe from the public.

INCORRECT_1.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_1.text: This is not the ideal choice. It lacks formality and structure.

INCORRECT_2.title: Not quite!
INCORRECT_2.text: This is not the ideal choice. It lacks formality and structure.

CORRECT.title: Correct!
CORRECT.text: This is a good decision. The meeting should be formally called to order to establish that it has begun.

ThinkAbout: How is information shared in a professional environment?
Does sharing this information put anyone at physical or reputational risk?
AskYourself: Just because you hear something, does that mean it's yours to share?
What responsibilities come with being part of a healthcare or athletic care team?

STEP_1.reportRational: In the healthcare field, you're expected to protect sensitive health and employment information of the patients you treat, demonstrating professional ethics, trustworthiness, and ethical responsibility.

STEP_2.instructions: After overhearing the conversation between Manny and the team coach you chose to send a text to your best friend sharing that Manny is about to be cut or will retire from the team. You felt safe doing so since you didn't post this information to a public site. This was not the ideal choice.
instructionsList: Consider what you know about legal and ethical issues. Select all the options that were violated.
Refer to the hint if you need guidance.
STEP_2.question: Which of the following legal and ethical issues were violated by this decision? (Select all that apply.)

Confidentiality.title: Correct!
Confidentiality.text: Patient confidentiality could have been violated by sharing private medical information with someone outside the patient's healthcare team.

Professional Ethics.title: Correct!
Professional Ethics.text: Professional ethics could have been violated by disclosing private information to someone outside the professional environment, compromising trust and conduct.

Malpractice.title: Not quite!
Malpractice.text: There was no occurrence of malpractice in this scenario. Use a hint if you need guidance.

Defamation.title: Not quite!
Defamation.text: There was no occurrence of defamation in this scenario. Use a hint if you need guidance.

hints.Confidentiality: Information about the patient that must remain private and can be shared only with other members of the patient's healthcare team.
hints.Professional Ethics: Professional ethics are guiding principles for how people and groups should interact with one another within a particular profession or business environment.
hints.Malpractice: Providing improper or unprofessional treatment or care that results in injury to another person.
hints.Defamation: Slander or libel; a false statement that causes ridicule or damage to a reputation.

STEP_2.reportRational: Legal and ethical considerations like professional ethics and confidentiality get violated by disclosing private medical information with someone outside the patient's healthcare team.
